LESSON: HUMAN RIGHTS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Political Systems
Topic 4.4: Human rights
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Human rights, part of Political Systems in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: which human rights are upheld in the society. 1. How does respect for human rights promote unity in society? 2. How are human rights upheld in society?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Human rights together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: A learner acquires the skill of sharing learnt knowledge as they engage a resource person in a

discussion on ways of promoting respect for human rights in the society.

• Digital literacy: A learner develops interactive skills as they use digital devices with assistive technology to find out

ways in which human rights are upheld in the society.

Values:
• Unity: Learners create charts or tactile charts in groups to illustrate categories of human rights and make a presentation.

• Social justice: Learners engage with a resource person in a discussion on ways in which human rights are violated in

society.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

62

• Assertiveness: Learners engage with a resource person in a discussion on ways in which human rights are violated in

society

• Self-awareness: A learner thinks and shares on human rights and responsibilities.

Link to other Learning Areas:

• Learners use the knowledge of Religious Studies to discern values such as ways of promoting respect for human rights in

the society as they engage with a Human rights officer.

• Learners use English/Kiswahili/KSL skills to role play scenarios that depict respect for human rights in the society.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Resource person, digital devices with assistive technology, charts, tactile charts, braille cards, approved appropriate print or

braille Social Studies Grade six textbook or other relevant materials.
